title: How to Use This Book
notes: This front-matter how-to is already dense, practical, and mostly clean: clear section heads, consistent first-person authorial voice in places, proper AsciiDoc/sym markup, no And/But/That sentence opens, no stock AI diction, and a strong closing method statement. The main defects are a vague pronoun whose antecedent is only implicit, a needless passive that breaks the surrounding first-person register, and a minor singular/plural slip on digital edition(s). No doctrine, scripture wording, or staging problems appear. Surgical fixes restore clarity and voice consistency without expanding the text.

proposals.old: Where it obscures a key word, I use a more literal rendering and say so, sometimes going beneath English to Hebrew or Greek, including unpointed Hebrew consonants where a second meaning stands inside the first.
proposals.new: Where the King James Version obscures a key word, I use a more literal rendering and say so, sometimes going beneath English to Hebrew or Greek, including unpointed Hebrew consonants where a second meaning stands inside the first.
proposals.summary: Replace the vague pronoun with its clear antecedent.
proposals.rationale: "It" has no explicit noun in the sentence; naming the King James Version removes the ambiguity while preserving the original claim and length.

proposals.old: It is an AI-assisted editorial estimate: Claude was asked to summarize common Christian readings and assign approximate shares, so read the numbers as relative consensus, not measurement.
proposals.new: It is an AI-assisted editorial estimate: I asked Claude to summarize common Christian readings and assign approximate shares, so read the numbers as relative consensus, not measurement.
proposals.summary: Restore first-person voice for the author's own editorial step.
proposals.rationale: The chapter already uses "I" and "my" for authorial choices; the passive "Claude was asked" is inconsistent and needlessly distant.

proposals.old: This book is offered in print and as a free digital edition.
proposals.new: This book is offered in print and as free digital editions.
proposals.summary: Match number with the following sentence.
proposals.rationale: The next sentence already says "digital editions" plural; aligning the count removes a small inconsistency.
